name: Tradeweb Markets Inc.
moat_justification: Dominant rates franchise with real network effects — over 50% institutional U.S. Treasury electronic share for nine consecutive quarters and a record 24.1% core risk (swaps) share — plus workflow embedding via AiEX automation and 54% EBITDA margins. Not 8+: credit is contested, wholesale Treasury share is slipping, fees per million are compressing on mix, and volumes ride market volatility.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality electronic-trading franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $110.68 it prices in the bull case: weighted IRR 13.29%, IV@15% $92.31; clears the 15% hurdle only at or below ~$92.
moat_for: Network effects — liquidity attracts liquidity; #1 in rates, >50% institutional U.S. Treasury share for nine straight quarters
Workflow embedding and switching costs — AiEX automation built into client trading workflows
Secular electronification tailwind, especially credit and international markets
Capital-light, high-margin model — 54.4% adjusted EBITDA margin, capex trivial vs OCF
moat_against: Fee compression — average fees per million fell double digits in swaps and cash credit in Q2 2026 on mix shift
Contested adjacencies — credit share fought over with MarketAxess/Bloomberg; wholesale Treasury revenue -1% YoY in Q2 2026
Volatility dependence — Q2 2026 revenue growth slowed to +9.0% as volatility normalized
Retail credit weakness — retail credit / muni revenue fell 22% in Q2 2026
